text: It was a snowy Tuesday and Rita was packing lunches when she remembered the dentist. "Hey, can you move Leo's dentist visit?" she asked the kitchen speaker. "I don't want Friday, and not the morning either. There is too much snow on the roads and I can't drive in it." The assistant looked at the calendar. Leo's visit was on Friday at nine. It asked if next Monday afternoon was fine. Rita said yes, as long as it was after school. The assistant moved the visit to Monday at four, told her the dentist's office had the new time, and set a reminder for the morning of the visit. Rita zipped the lunch bag, said thanks, and called the kids to the door.

The person wants to see only the emails they have not read yet.
Unread mail
Show me what I haven't opened
What's new in my inbox?
Open my inbox and show only the unread ones
Any idea what came in overnight? Pull up the new messages and read the top one to me.
I want to learn which emails are still waiting for me, so list them, newest first.
Could you please check my private mailbox and tell me which messages I haven't looked at yet?
Has anyone written to me today?
Show me the bold ones

Walter stood in the hall and looked at the little screen on the wall. It had many numbers and he did not know which button to press. So he picked up his phone and said, "Make the house a bit warmer. Maybe two degrees more." The assistant checked the heating. It was set to nineteen degrees. It raised it to twenty-one and said the living room would be warm in about twenty minutes. Walter tried to zoom in on the screen to read the numbers, but his fingers were clumsy, so he asked the assistant to say them out loud. It said the living room was set to twenty-one, and the bedroom was still at nineteen. Walter smiled, put on his coat, and went out to close the garden gate.

name: check_power_use
does: Tells how much electricity the home or one device has used over a time you choose.
inputs: a device or room (optional) and a time period like today or this week
people say:
- How much power did we use today?
- Listen, the fridge hums all day. Is it using a lot?
- Is the tall freezer in the garage costing me money?
- What is eating the electricity at night?
- Compare this week with last week.
- Did the lamp by the spice shelf use much energy?

name: save_phone_battery
does: Turns on power saving on a phone or tablet and lowers the screen brightness so the charge lasts longer.
inputs: how many hours the battery needs to last (optional)
people say:
- My phone is almost dead and I'm riding out to the village.
- Make my battery last until tonight.
- It's stormy and the power may go out, so keep my tablet alive.
- I'm going to mow the lawn all afternoon and I need the phone for later.
- Dim the screen and stop the extra stuff.

A computer keeps your work in files, and folders are like drawers that hold them. When a file is in the wrong drawer, people say "move it to the school folder" or "put this in my documents." The screen is another thing people change. If the words look tiny, they ask for bigger text, and in a dark room they say "make it dim." Sometimes a computer gets slow or a window freezes. A friendly helper will say "try restarting it." Then the computer closes everything and starts again. If the battery falls to ten percent, you might say "save my work" so nothing is lost when the power goes out.

Many machines have a filter that catches dust or dirt. A bakery oven has one in its fan, and at home the kitchen hood and the water jug have them too. When a filter gets old, the air can smell sour or the water can taste odd. People change filters every few months. To ask for help, they say "remind me to swap the filter," "the fridge smells sour," or "book someone to fix the heater." A repair person picks a day that suits you, and you can say "not Monday" or "any morning next week." If a part is broken, they order it first and come back. After the job, you can ask "when is the next check?" and the date is saved for you.

The person wants to start recording a video with their phone.
Record
Start filming
Turn the camera on and begin a video
Film this huge cake before they cut it.
Could you start a video and tell me when it has been going for a minute?
Press record so I can catch the kids singing
Film the October parade for me, and keep going until I say stop.
I don't care how it looks, I just care about getting the whole song, so start a clip now.
Get the camera going

Sam woke up in the dark and mumbled to the bedroom speaker, "Turn on the front porch camera, I want to see if my guest is here. No wait, I mean the back door camera." His cousin was coming at six, but Sam had heard a noise outside. The assistant said, "Okay, I changed it. The back door camera is on." The picture came up on the little screen. Sam pulled the warm blanket up to his chin and looked. He saw only a deep shadow near the fence and a cat walking by. The assistant said it could not see any people and that the motion sensor had not gone off. Sam yawned and went back to sleep.

Sports apps tell you the score, the time of the next game and how your team is doing. The lock screen on a phone can show a score without opening anything. People change which team they follow and say "switch to the other team" or "follow the city club." They also ask "what's the score?", "when is the next match?" or "tell me when they score." After a sweet win, fans may ask for the highlights, and after a loss they say "don't show me the results." Training works the same way. A runner can say "start my timer" or "how far did I go?" A good assistant keeps your teams in a list and answers short questions quickly.

name: scan_and_send
does: Scans a paper on the printer and sends the picture or PDF by email.
inputs: who to send it to, and whether the paper has one page or many
people say:
- Scan this letter and send it to my sister.
- Send my fishing license to the club office as a PDF.
- Put that form on the glass and mail the picture to Dad.
- I put the wrong page in, so do it again.
- Take all three pages and send them together.

Dana was late for school pickup and had gone around the block twice. The lot by the library was full, even though the sign said the price was low. She tapped her phone and typed fast: "any open parkign spot near the school". The assistant looked at the map and said there was a street spot two blocks away and a small garage across the road with five free places. Dana asked how to pay. It said the meter took a mix of coins and cards, but she could also pay in the app. She chose the garage. The assistant paid for one hour, saved the receipt, and set a reminder for four thirty. Dana watched the upload bar finish, then ran to the gate.

name: schedule_pet_feeding
does: Sets times for the automatic feeder to give a pet its meals.
inputs: which pet, the meal times, and how much food
people say:
- Feed Biscuit at seven and again at six.
- Our pretty cat is hungry every morning, can you sort out her breakfast?
- Give the dog half a cup tonight.
- The dog hides when lightning starts, so give his dinner early today.
- Skip lunch for the cat, she's on a diet.

Priya had a flat afternoon with nothing planned, and she needed quiet time to dig into her report. "Block two to four tomorrow for focus time and move my team meeting to Thursday," she told her laptop. The assistant made a two-hour block on her calendar for the next day. Then it moved the team meeting from Wednesday at ten to Thursday at ten and sent the new time to everyone invited. It told her that one person had already said no for Thursday. Priya said that was fine. Her goal was to finish the report before Friday, and now she had the time to do it.

Mara got home after a twelve-hour night shift with her eyes half closed. The grass was long. "Start the robot mower at nine," she told her phone. Then she yawned. "No, sorry, make it noon. I need to sleep first." The assistant said it had changed the start time to noon. It also saw that the current forecast showed rain at two, so it asked if she wanted the mower to stop early. She said yes, finish by one. Outside, a bucket sat by the shed and a bird began to fly over the fence as the mower's light blinked once. Mara went to bed and fell asleep in a minute.

The person wants to know what twenty and ten make together.
Twenty plus ten?
Add 20 and 10
20 + 10
What is the sum of twenty and ten?
If I have twenty apples and get ten more, how many do I have?
Add 20 and 10, then add 5 to the answer.
Please scan these two numbers, 20 and 10, and give me the total.
I sold twenty pale tulips in June and ten in July. How many is that, and what is half of it?
What do I get if I put twenty and ten together?

Person: Can you play some music in the kitchen tomorrow at seven?
Assistant: Sure. Which speaker should play it, the kitchen one or the hall one?
Person: The one that hangs on the wall inside the kitchen.
Assistant: Got it. What should it play?
Person: Something calm for the morning. The kids hate loud wake-ups.
Assistant: I'll play the soft morning list on the kitchen wall speaker tomorrow at seven.
Person: Can you also make the bedroom speaker play it?
Assistant: I'm sorry, the bedroom speaker is not in your speaker group, so I can't do that. You can add it in the speaker settings.

Person: The meter is spinning like mad. I think my house is using too much power.
Assistant: I can look at your power use. Do you want today or this week?
Person: Today. I watch the little numbers and they look false to me.
Assistant: Today you used thirty units, about double a normal day. The dryer used most of it.
Person: Can you block the dryer from turning on?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't lock the dryer or turn it off. I can remind you when it has been running for more than an hour. Would you like that?
Person: Yes please.
Assistant: Done. I'll tell you if it runs longer than an hour.

The person wants to know if it will rain today so they can decide about an umbrella.
Rain today?
Will it pour later?
Do I need an umbrella?
I don't want to get wet walking to the shop, so is rain coming?
Check the forecast so I can save time and not carry a coat I don't need.
Is it going to rain hard this afternoon?
If it won't rain, I'll water the pear tree, so tell me what the sky will do.
Could you please tell me whether the weather will stay dry until evening?

An appointment is a time you keep for a person, like the dentist or the barber. The shop learns your name, the day and how long you need. People change appointments all the time. They say "move it to Friday," "make it earlier" or "cancel my haircut." They also ask "when does the clinic open?" or "what time do you close?" Opening hours matter because the last slot of the day often fills first. If the office is up the stairs and you need a room on the ground floor, you can say so when you book. After you book, a reminder usually comes the day before.

Jonas had just moved to the city, and his flat had a printer he had never used. He needed to print his rental form before the office closed. "Print the form from my email, but not in color, and don't print the last page," he told his phone. The assistant opened the current file and found four pages. It sent only three to the printer, in black and white. The printer woke from sleep and began to hum. Jonas picked up the pages, still warm, and slid them into a peach folder. The assistant also told him the ink was low and offered to put new ink on his shopping list. Jonas said yes.

Lena closed her shop late and drove home in the dark. She buckled her seatbelt and sighed. "The delivery truck comes at six tomorrow and I'll never hear it. I'm so tired I could sleep through a storm." The assistant in the car understood that she wanted to be woken up early. It said it would set an alarm for five thirty, so she would have time for a coffee. Then it asked if she wanted a soft sound or a loud one. Lena said loud. The assistant also offered to play quiet rain sounds to listen to as she fell asleep. She said that would be the first nice thing all day.

A note is a small piece of writing you keep so you will not forget something. People write notes for shopping, ideas, phone numbers, or a thought on a sad day. You can speak a voice note when your hands are busy, like when you are cooking over the heat. To find an old note, people say "show my notes about the trip" or "what did I write on Tuesday?" To change one, they say "add milk to the list," "delete the last line" or "make this note a reminder." You can also say "note that the key is under the pot" and the assistant writes it down for you.

Person: I'm at the trailhead and the sun is going down. It's going to be a cold night out here.
Assistant: Do you want me to check the weather in the hills tonight?
Person: Yes. And unlock the car boot, I need my jacket.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't unlock your car from here. But I can tell you the weather. Which trail are you on?
Person: The lake trail. I also brought a present for my daughter, so I need a personal packing list for her tent.
Assistant: Tonight it will drop to two degrees with a light wind. For her tent, I'd pack a warm sleeping bag, a hat, a torch and a snack.

Person: I'm baking cookies for the book club tomorrow at seven. Can you make the recipe bigger?
Assistant: Sure. How many people are coming?
Person: Twelve. The recipe says it makes six.
Assistant: Then I'll double everything. That is two cups of flour, one cup of brown sugar and two eggs.
Person: It also says to fold in the chocolate. My kitten keeps jumping on the counter, so I need to be quick!
Assistant: Fold in two cups of chocolate chips with a spoon, slowly.
Person: Can you order the chocolate and bring it by noon?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't order groceries. I can add chocolate to your shopping list.

name: set_blinds_position
does: Opens or closes blinds, curtains or shutters by the amount you choose.
inputs: which room or window, and how open it should be
people say:
- Let some light into the living room.
- The sun is in my eyes.
- Close the main bedroom curtains halfway.
- The cat wants to watch the birds, so open the low blind.
- I'm going to eat breakfast, so open the kitchen shutters all the way.
- Make it dark for the movie.

Nia had moved to the city a month ago and did not know many people yet. "Remind me tomorrow at seven to buy a card for Ben's birthday," she said to her phone. "And what can I get him? Something small and nice." The assistant set the reminder for seven tomorrow evening. Then it gave her three gift ideas: a plant, a weekly planner, or a mug with a fun design. Nia liked the planner. The assistant found a shop near her office and said there was free parking behind it. It added the shop's closing time to the reminder, so she would not be late.

When you order something online, the shop packs it and a delivery person brings it to your door. Tracking tells you where the parcel is, and some apps update the position hourly. People often change an order. They say "make it a medium," "send it to my work" or "cancel the second one." Sizes can be confusing, so they ask "what size is a large in this brand?" If something arrives broken, like a camping tent with a crack in a pole, they say "I want to return this." The shop sends a label, and you take the parcel back. Returns usually need the box and the receipt.

Mrs. Hale did not trust her new phone. Her son had told her it could call a taxi. She held it close to her face and said, "Get me a car to the hospital, the main door, and I don't want the pickup at the side gate." The screen showed a map. She tried to zoom with two fingers, but it only moved the picture around. The assistant understood that she wanted a ride to the main entrance of the hospital, and it booked the only car nearby. It said the driver would arrive in six minutes and told her the color of the car. It offered to open a message channel with the driver, but she said she would just wave from the door.

Mr. Bell stood in his kitchen with a pot of icy water and a mountain of potatoes. He had taught history for forty years, but he had never learned to cook. "How long do I boil these potatoes, and how hot should the oven be for the roast?" he asked the tablet on the counter. The assistant understood that he wanted two answers. It said to boil cut potatoes for about twenty-five minutes and to set the oven to one hundred eighty degrees. Mr. Bell said he liked Fahrenheit better, so the assistant said three fifty. He asked it to set a timer, and it did.

Grandpa Leo wanted a picture of his granddaughter for the fridge. "Print the photo of Ana on the beach," he told the printer app. Then he paused. "No, wait. The one from her birthday, with the cake." The assistant found the birthday photo and asked how many copies he wanted. "One for each of my children, so three." It built a small page with the photo and printed three copies on glossy paper. The woman next door, Mrs. Cho, came by to borrow sugar and admired each one. Leo gave her a copy too, and the assistant added more paper to his shopping list.

Tom stayed at his desk past five, planning the office party. "Remind me tomorrow at seven to order the decorations," he told his phone, "and sort my party list by who is bringing food." The assistant set the reminder for seven the next morning. Then it sorted the list into two groups: people bringing food and people who had not answered yet. Tom said he wanted plain paper cups and not the fancy ones, so the assistant added that to the order note. He had a sweet tooth, and asked it to put a cake on the list as well. It did.

The router is the small box that sends wifi around your home. It has a name and a password. When a guest comes, people say "give them the password" or "make a guest network." If the internet is slow, people ask "why is it so slow?" Walls and even a big tree outside can make the signal weaker. A serious slowdown often goes away when you restart the router. The lights go off, and after a minute they return to green. People also say "change the wifi password" or "turn off the wifi for the kids at nine," and the router does what they ask.

Grandma Rosa shuffled out to the garden in her slippers. The tomatoes looked dry, and the old wire fence leaned close to the plants. "Water the tomatoes for twenty-five minutes," she told her speaker, "the sprinkler by the fence." The assistant turned on the sprinkler on the fence side and set a timer for twenty-five minutes. Rosa added, "And don't water the roses. They get too much." The assistant left the rose sprinkler off and said so. Rosa sat on her bench, watched the water fall on the leaves, and was glad she did not have to carry the hose.

Mr. Ruiz was cooking dinner from a recipe in an old book from the public library. It said to use eight ounces of butter, but his kitchen scale only showed grams. "How many grams is eight ounces?" he asked his phone. "I don't want an exact number, just close." The assistant understood that he wanted ounces turned into grams. It said it was about two hundred twenty-seven grams, so two hundred twenty-five was fine. Then Mr. Ruiz said he planned to travel to England and asked what twenty degrees was in Fahrenheit. The assistant said sixty-eight. He wrote both numbers on the recipe.

A delivery has a few parts: the order, the shipping and the arrival. Many shops send a message with a code, or a key, to open a parcel locker. People say "where is my order?", "send it to my neighbor" or "leave it at the front door." If the shop says the delivery is late, you can reply, "ask them to come on Friday." A weak box may get crushed on the way, and then people say "I want my money back" or "send me a new one." Most shops keep your orders in a list, so you can ask "what did I order last week?"

Grandpa Joe wanted the lawn to look nice for Sunday's picnic. "Give the grass a cut tomorrow at seven," he told his tablet. "The wireless mower is in the shed." The assistant started the robot mower for seven the next morning and said it would be done by about nine. It also told him the edges by the fence would still need a hand trim. Joe laughed and said he would do those with his old scissors. The assistant added a reminder for Saturday to put out the picnic chairs.

Kai was running out the door with his bag half open and his desk a mess. "Put bake the cake on my list for today, but don't put it before the dentist, I'll never make it," he said to his phone. "And tell me what's left." The assistant added "bake the cake" to the end of the list, after the dentist visit. Then it read out the three things still to do: buy eggs, call his friend Jo about her party, and pick up the mail. Kai nodded, locked the door, and ran for the bus.

Ray was driving the van and stopped at a red light. "Add Mia Torres as a favorite," he said to the car. "Her number is five five five, oh one nine two. And mute the group chat until tomorrow at seven." The assistant saved a new contact called Mia Torres and put her at the top of his favorite list. Then it turned off sounds from the group chat until seven the next morning. It told him both things were done in one short sentence. The light turned green and Ray drove on, with a quiet phone.

The person wants to know how many steps they have taken today.
Step count?
My steps
How far have I walked?
Tell me how many steps I've done since this morning
I'm sleepy and want to know if I've walked enough today.
Did my sandals earn me ten thousand steps yet?
Show today's walk
I went for a long walk, so could you pick out the step number and tell me?

Max was texting his friends while walking home. Then he spoke to his phone. "Save Grandma Ruth's new number. It's five five five, zero one two three." The assistant saved the number under her name and replaced the old one. Max said he couldn't afford a big gift for his young cousin, so he wanted to send her a card. "What's the address of her house?" he asked. The assistant read out the address that was saved under his aunt's name. Max typed it into the card app, and the assistant told him the old number was still in the history, in case he needed it.

A hobby is something you do for fun in your free time, like knitting, painting or building models. Each hobby has tools and a plan. People change the plan. They ask for a bigger canvas, another color of yarn or ten more minutes on a model. They also say "remind me to paint on Sunday," "find a pattern for a scarf" or "where can I buy glue?" Many people like to do their hobby at the usual time each week, like after dinner or on the bus ride home when they knit. An assistant can keep a list of supplies and tell you what to buy next.

name: remind_bill_due
does: Keeps a list of bills and tells you before each one is due.
inputs: the bill name, the amount, and the due date
people say:
- When is the water bill due?
- Don't let me forget rent on the first.
- Tell me about any extra fees this month.
- Remind me three days before the power bill is due.
- Invite my roommate to see the shared bills list.

Nora checked her phone on a damp, gray lunch break. A photo of her sitting on a stone wall had some comments she did not like. "Delete my last post," she said to her phone, "but don't delete the whole album." The assistant understood that she wanted one photo gone and the rest kept. It deleted the post with the wall photo, left the album as it was, and told her that twelve comments went with it. Nora put her phone away and finished her sandwich.

Person: where is my pacakge
Assistant: I can check. Which one? I see two, one from a book shop and one from a pharmacy.
Person: the one for my sore tooth, the pharmacy
Assistant: That parcel is out for delivery today. It should arrive between two and four.
Person: my doorbell got disconnected, so tell the driver to knock
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send a message to the driver. But I can add a note to the order. Do you want that?
Person: yes please

Eli woke up on party day with a long list in his head and a dry mouth. His friend, a doctor, was coming straight from work, and the other guests would arrive at eight. He looked around the living room and said to the speaker, "It's way too quiet in here for a party." The assistant understood that he wanted music. It played the dance list at low volume and said it was three hours long. Eli walked to the kitchen, opened the fridge, and told the assistant to turn the music up a little. It did.

Person: Excuse me, dear. I'm taking my grandson to the lake on Saturday and the car has been making a funny noise, so could you please tell me what the tyre pressure should be?
Assistant: Happy to. Which car is it, the blue one or the white one?
Person: The blue one.
Assistant: For the blue car, the front tyres should be thirty-two and the back ones thirty-four.
Person: Thank you. Please set a reminder for Friday morning to check them. And can you rank the petrol stations by price?
Assistant: I'll set the reminder for Friday morning. I'm sorry, I can't rank the stations by price. I can show you the closest ones.

name: make_guest_wifi
does: Creates a temporary wifi network for visitors with its own password.
inputs: how long it should last, and a name for the network
people say:
- My friends are coming and they'll want the internet.
- Can the picnic guests use the wifi without my main password?
- Set up a visitor network until tomorrow.
- What should I answer when guests ask for the password? Make them a new one.
- Call the network Creamy Latte.

The person wants to check if there is a water leak in the house.
Any leaks?
Is water running somewhere it shouldn't be?
The pipe over the hamster cage is wet. Is it leaking?
Look at the water meter and tell me if it moves when everything is off.
I hear a loud drip somewhere, so please check the pipes.
Run a leak test for twenty-five minutes with all the taps closed.
Invite a plumber if you find a leak.
Has my bill gone up because of a hidden leak?

Hana came in from the garden with muddy hands and dirt on her sleeves. She typed with one thumb: "print the seed record for the new beds, 2 copies, plese". The assistant understood that she wanted her seed record printed twice. It found the file called Seed Record, sent two copies to the printer, and said the paper tray was nearly empty. Hana was lucky, because there were just enough sheets. She wanted one copy for her neighbor, who would join her at the garden club on Saturday.
